sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Home Hydroponics and Gardening Equipment

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU Regulatory Framework for Direct Investment Screening (Regulation (EU) 2019/452)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 25 March 2020 implementing UBO disclosure obligations; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 on the fight against money laundering, as amended; Luxembourg Law of 26 February 2021 implementing EU Directive 2018/843 (AMLD5) and subsequent CJEU case law restricting public access to beneficial ownership data.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity card of each partner, general partner, and natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent state authority in the country of origin (e.g., police, passport office, civil registry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address / recent utility bill or bank statement for each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issued by utility provider or recognized financial institution in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or notarially certified partnership deed / private deed of the SCSp (acte de société), including all annexes and UBO declarations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Luxembourg notary or executing partner (if private form permitted under the limited partnership statute)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and natural-person UBOs against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) watchlists, CSSF consolidated sanctions and regulatory measures, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EC) No. 881/2002), UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and recognized PEP databases. Screening must occur prior to notarization, on update of ownership, and at least annually thereafter. Adverse or ambiguous hits require enhanced due diligence and, where necessary, refusal of incorporation or dissolution of the SCSp in accordance with the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in any language using Latin-alphabet characters. Names in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese) must be transliterated into Latin characters for registration. The legal form suffix 'SCSp' must appear in the name. The name must not be misleading, contrary to Luxembourg public policy, or create a likelihood of confusion with existing trademarks or registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon administrative rejection by the RCS, the applicant or authorized counsel must file a written administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Minister of Justice within two calendar months from the rejection notice. The appeal must include the proposed name, evidence of no prior conflicting registration, evidence of lawful entitlement, and a reasoned rebuttal of the rejection ground. Interim remedy is available before the administrative courts, and notarial or legal counsel representation is required. Name reservation extensions are not automatically granted; after twenty-nine days the applicant may submit a new request for re-reservation with a fresh confirmation from the proposed entity and renewed AML/CFT due diligence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for a SCSp engaged in online retail of garden hydroponics and home equipment. A licensed domiciliation agent may provide a registered office in Luxembourg, provided that physical access to books and records is possible during normal business hours and the office is not used only as a mail-forwarding address. Commercial substance requirements of the Luxembourg transfer-pricing rules and substance circulars apply; the SCSp should have adequate economic activities, decision-making presence, and records at the registered office for any pass-through tax election or EU benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Risk_Standard – approximate 12% likelihood of unannounced on-site inspection during the first 24 months after incorporation for a low-risk e-commerce entity, rising to 25% if the SCSp uses a virtual/domiciliation office without local operational records or if UBO profiles trigger enhanced due diligence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation application fee
Notarization of partnership deed and annexes (before Luxembourg notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff based on nominal capital and services performed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration of SCSp (commercial registry inscription and filings)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing for UBO disclosure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulatory filing – no current fee for initial UBO declaration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC and sanctions screening of partners and natural-person UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: CSF-Consultants / designated AML counsel and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for comprehensive sanctions and PEP screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate legal opinion on SCSp pass-through eligibility and name clearance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for pre-incorporation legal opinion and structuring

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization of foreign identity and address documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Embassy, consulate, or apostille-issuing authority in document origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular and diplomatic fee schedule plus courier charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic publication of incorporation notice in the Legal Gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés – RESA)
Domiciliation agent fee for registered office in Luxembourg (first year, if virtual office permitted)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk e-commerce entities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incidental contingency for exchange rate, courier, and specialized compliance documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No fixed statutory basis; internal fee policy

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 101-103 (Special Limited Partnership / SCSp); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and Annual Accounts; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic filing via myguichet.lu (eJustice/eID or Luxtrust authenticated).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (partnership agreement / contrat de société) — executed either as a notarial deed or as private writing with legalized signatures, deposited with the RCS for registration and publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital requirement for an SCSp; contributions (cash or in kind) are freely set in the partnership agreement. No escrow account or notarized capital certificate is required under Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [SCSp] (FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION). Adopted by the General Partner, acting as manager, on [date]. 1. The form of a société en commandite spéciale is confirmed; the partnership agreement is approved and adopted. 2. The subscriptions of all partners are accepted; any capital contributions are recorded without escrow or minimum capital requirement. 3. The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg; the General Partner is authorized to file the statutes with the RCS and to arrange the publication in the RESA. 4. [Name] is appointed manager with full signatory authority. 5. The manager is authorized to open bank accounts and to execute the payment service agreements with Stripe and PayPal. Signed: [General Partner].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Luxembourg) or legal counsel; if private writing, signatures certified by a notary or the respective consulate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement in French or English, including the corporate name, registered office in Luxembourg, duration, object, contribution schedule, UBO declarations, and management powers of the General Partner. Execute the deed before a notary or by private writing with legalized signatures; retain an executed original for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all partners and the General Partner
Proof of residential address of each partner
Lease or domiciliation agreement for the Luxembourg registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel requests amendments, revise the draft and re-execute; for signature legalization issues, obtain a new certified signature page and a certificate of signature authenticity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Initial Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., ING Luxembourg, BGL BNP Paribas, Spuerkeess) or authorized electronic money institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit KYC and AML documentation for all partners and the manager; obtain an IBAN; deposit any agreed initial contributions. Since an SCSp has no minimum capital, a blocked account is not required; record contributions in the partnership accounts.
required_dossiers: UBO and KYC forms (AML/CFT due diligence)
Brief business plan and source of funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional information, provide a source-of-wealth declaration and a tax residency certificate; concurrently open a standby account with a second bank to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS online service via myguichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in with Luxtrust/eID, complete the standard incorporation form for an SCSp, upload the notarized or legally certified statutes, and pay the EUR 75 (approx. USD 85) filing fee. The RCS issues the registration extract (extrait du RCS) and the official RCS number upon approval.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the executed partnership agreement
Identification documents of the General Partner and manager
Notarized power of attorney (if filed by an agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a formal query, rectify the statutes within one month by an amending deed or submit a written explanatory response; appeal a refusal to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RESA publication service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration data to the RESA for publication. Verify the electronic publication notice and retain the confirmation as proof of third-party effectiveness.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or refused, contact the LBR helpdesk; request an expedited correction via the RCS online portal and re-confirm the publication date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial owner declaration within 30 days of incorporation, identifying all natural persons owning or controlling more than 25% of the partnership interests. Submit the online RBE form with supporting documents and pay the filing fee.
required_dossiers: Copy of the executed partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE queries the declaration, submit a corrected return promptly; late or inaccurate filings trigger fines — engage legal counsel immediately to normalize the record.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No operating license is required for ISIC 4791 online retail. General product safety and market surveillance authority: ILNAS (Luxembourg Institute for Standardisation, Accreditation, Safety and Quality of Products and Services); Ministry of the Economy (General Directorate for Industry) for any future warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — statutory license exemption for pure e-commerce retail of garden hydroponics equipment; a Category-1 commodo declaration under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 applies only if a physical warehouse or assembly facility is established.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — online distribution of gardening/hydroponics equipment is not a classified installation under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments; no EIA report or environmental permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC thresholds apply. As a distributor, comply with EU WEEE Directive (2012/19/EU), RoHS Directive (2011/65/EU), and Packaging Directive (94/62/EC) — register as a producer/importer via a national WEEE compliance scheme and provide take-back labelling for electrical equipment and batteries.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the administrative registered office, no fire brigade permit is required unless the premises are open to the public; comply with Règlement grand-ducal of 4 November 1994 for fire safety of commercial premises. If a warehouse is operated, obtain a fire safety certificate, structural load clearance, and a workplace inspection under the Luxembourg Labour Code (Code du travail) and Council Directive 89/654/EEC.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Direct Tax Authority for corporate/personal income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax (portal: impotsdirects.public.lu); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) — Indirect/Direct registration authority for VAT and registration duties (portal: aed.public.lu); unified e-government filing portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu (professional eSpace); company registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL), portal: lbr.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1 — Incorporate the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL), obtain the notarial deed, appoint a general partner (associé commandité) and make the required deposit; the RCSL issues the registration number (matricule / numéro de registre). STEP 2 — Apply for the tax identification number (numéro d'identification fiscale) with the ACD by filing the standard registration data for the SCSp and for any partner who is a Luxembourg resident taxpayer; the ACD issues the matricule fiscale used for direct tax declarations. STEP 3 — Register for VAT with the AED by filing the VAT registration declaration (formulaire d'immatriculation / déclaration d'activité) together with the RCS extract, the partnership agreement, identity documents of the general partner and the manager details; the AED issues the Luxembourg VAT number with the LU prefix (numéro de TVA). STEP 4 — A foreign (non-established) entity with taxable operations in Luxembourg must register directly with the AED, or use the One-Stop-Shop (OSS/IOSS) for distance sales, or appoint an accredited VAT representative (mandataire assujetti à la TVA) where required; each non-resident partner without a Luxembourg civic number must also complete the simplified ACD registration to receive an individual Luxembourg tax number before filing partnership allocations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax purposes; the partnership itself is not subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) or net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune); partnership profits and losses flow through to partners in proportion to their entitlement and are taxed at partner level — Luxembourg-resident corporate and non-corporate partners on worldwide income, non-resident partners on Luxembourg-source income attributable to their Luxembourg participation; the SCSp remains fully subject to VAT registration and filing obligations as a taxable person for indirect tax purposes. No Luxembourg tax-free zone or special economic processing zone applies to the SCSp; territoriality is the standard residence/worldwide regime for Luxembourg residents and source-based for non-residents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) §175bis LIR optional election: a Luxembourg commercial partnership (including an SCSp) whose partners are exclusively fully taxable corporate bodies or Luxembourg permanent establishments of foreign companies may irrevocably elect to be treated as a resident capital company, causing opaque entity-level corporation tax (available only upon prior written option, binding on all partners and subsequent years); (b) VAT small-enterprise waiver: renouncement of the Art. 146bis VAT Law €35,000 small-business exemption so as to apply normal VAT and recover input VAT; (c) e-commerce special schemes: election to register under the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for intra-EU distance sales and the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) for low-value consignments; (d) transfer pricing and ATAD hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory statutory responses rather than elective check-the-box mechanisms — Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; foreign-law entities are functionally classified as transparent or opaque under domestic law and double-tax-treaty allocation rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); prudential and AML/CFT supervision for credit institutions and payment/e-money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). The BCL acts as Luxembourg’s central bank and member of the Eurosystem.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area Member State. Under Article 63 TFEU and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements, both current and capital transactions are freely convertible and may be repatriated without prior exchange-control approval. There are no exchange-control restrictions on inbound equity subscription, operating working capital, loan repayments, dividend/profit allocations to non-resident partners, or trade settlements. The SCSp is treated as a contractual partnership for Luxembourg tax purposes, so no Luxembourg withholding tax applies on distributions to qualifying non-resident partners. The only legal impediments arise from EU sanctions and asset-freeze measures, anti-money-laundering obligations, and bank KYC requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion ratio, or repatriation deadline for export proceeds from the online sale of garden hydroponics and household gardening equipment. Export receipts may be held freely in EUR or foreign currency and converted at market rates. Banks are required only to report cross-border payment statistics to the BCL under the euro-area balance-of-payments regime for official statistical purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. An EEA-licensed e-money institution or payment institution registered in the EEA and passporting into Luxembourg under the revised Payment Services Directive may provide euro IBAN accounts, merchant acquiring, online payouts, and limited FX conversion for a cross-border e-commerce treasury. However, EMIs cannot extend commercial credit, offer traditional deposit products, or serve as a full-service corporate bank; funds held through an EMI are safeguarding accounts rather than bank deposits. Offshore third-country EMIs are not viable for routine Luxembourg treasury operations due to EU licensing constraints and CSSF/FIU reporting expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML/CFT law does not impose a blanket in-person interview requirement, but banks must identify and verify the SCSp and its beneficial owners using reliable independent sources. Most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks permit remote onboarding via video call and eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures, with the final acceptance always based on internal risk appetite. In practice, a Luxembourg registered office, a notarised or written partnership agreement, and an authorised local representative with power of attorney are required. If any partner is resident in a high-risk third country or the corporate structure shows unusual complexity, a physical investor or board interview may be required before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership with non-resident SPVs or tax-optimisation structures as limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), SCSp partnership deed, notarised limited partnership agreement, full ownership chart, UBO declaration forms, passports and proof of address for all partners, corporate certificates of good standing, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements, and a written memorandum explaining the commercial purpose of the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce income via Stripe and PayPal without an established banking/credit history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year business plan with projected cash flows, website and online marketplace details, merchant acquiring and platform contracts, customer KYC/AML procedures, expected transaction volume and average ticket sizes, refund and chargeback policy, PCI-DSS compliance evidence, and current management accounts if any are available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to suppliers in jurisdictions that differ from the invoicing entity or from the ultimate consignee's country
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply contracts, purchase orders, vendor invoices, Incoterms on transport documents, pro-forma commercial invoices, customs and export declarations, ultimate consignee confirmation, bank reference for the SCSp, and a group treasury memorandum explaining the payment routing and containing a sanctions and beneficial-ownership risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution or subscription amount originating from a third-country bank with no prior Luxembourg nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement or credit confirmation identifying the remitter, board resolution of the SCSp authorising the capital call, partner subscription agreement, partner source-of-funds declaration, underlying commercial documentation supporting the transfer, and a written undertaking to provide complete balance-of-payments documentation to the BCL through the bank if requested.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The SCSp must receive partner capital contributions into a bank account opened in its own name at a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution. The remitter sends a SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR transfers or a SEPA / SEPA Instant credit transfer for EUR payments, with the payment's remittance information field containing the SCSp's legal name, Luxembourg business registration number, and the reference 'Capital contribution' or 'SCSp equity subscription'. Luxembourg applies no exchange-control permit requirement; however, the bank requires a copy of the capital call, the limited partnership agreement, and identification of the contributor before crediting the funds. For contributions sourced from shareholder loans, a loan confirmation must be provided to enable subsequent operational disbursement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outgoing trade settlements are executed over (i) SWIFT MT103 cover payments for direct vendor wire transfers in overseas currencies, (ii) documentary and commercial letters of credit opened via SWIFT MT700 messages for supplier trade finance, (iii) SWIFT MT202 or MT202COV for bank-to-bank interbank transfers, (iv) SEPA credit transfers for euro-zone suppliers, and (v) intra-company transfers using SWIFT messages between the SCSp's own accounts. Every disbursement should be supported by a supplier invoice, purchase order, and, where applicable, transport and customs documentation. Payment platforms should enforce dual-signatory authorisation above defined thresholds and integrate automated sanctions/AML screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign exchange transactions with licensed credit institutions
Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted settlement infrastructure
Exchange-traded and OTC currency options used solely for hedging underlying commercial exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary of RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of up to EUR 5,000; risk of judicial dissolution and strike-off if persistent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the annual confirmation reminder, generally on the RCS registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to EUR 1,250; repeated non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, due by 31 March for the previous calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 0.8% per month; enforced collection through garnishment; denial of CC certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit required if the SCSp qualifies as a large undertaking, i.e. exceeds two of: balance sheet total EUR 4.4M, net turnover EUR 8.8M, average employees 50; otherwise exempt, but may be required by the partnership agreement or at the request of a partner.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP; IFRS permitted in accordance with EU Regulation 1606/2002; SCSp is tax-transparent so no corporate income tax filing, only partner-level aggregation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of the accuracy of beneficial ownership data filed via the LBR online portal; any shareholding transfer or beneficial ownership change must be filed within 30 days. Confirmation due within 30 days after the annual reminder, on the RCS registration anniversary.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% headline CIT for taxable income exceeding EUR 200,000 (progressive schedule: 15% up to EUR 175,000; 16% on EUR 175,001 - EUR 200,000; 17% above EUR 200,000). Default SCSp status is fiscally transparent: no CIT is charged at the partnership level; each partner is taxed on its allocable share. If the SCSp validly elects to be subject to CIT under Art. 175bis LIR, the aggregate corporate burden in Luxembourg City is 24.94% (17% CIT + 1.19% employment fund surcharge equal to 7% of the CIT base + 6.75% municipal business tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: (1) IP Box (Art. 50bis LIR): 80% exemption on qualifying net IP income, producing an effective CIT rate of approx. 5.04% for opted-in entities; transparent partners receive the benefit pro rata. (2) Participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividend income and capital gains where the corporate partner holds at least 10% or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 6,000,000 of the distributing entity's capital, with a 12-month holding period and a subject-to-tax condition. (3) R&D tax credit (Art. 152quater LIR): up to 20% of eligible R&D expenditure, capped at EUR 1,500,000 per tax year. (4) Investment tax credit of 8% - 13% on eligible qualifying assets. (5) 0% withholding tax on outbound interest and royalty payments. (6) Unlimited tax loss carry-forward.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiration; utilization requires continuity of the same commercial activity and remains subject to the AED anti-abuse assessment)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 8000 (declaration pour l'impot sur le revenu des collectivites et pour l'impot commercial communal) filed electronically via the eCDF portal on MyGuichet.lu using LuxTrust or national eID authentication. This form applies when the SCSp has exercised the Art. 175bis LIR option to be taxed as a corporate entity and to corporate partners reporting their allocated SCSp income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (calendar or commercial fiscal year; initial, final and partial-period returns pro-rated).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May following the end of the fiscal year (e.g. FY ending 31 December 2024 due 31 May 2025); the AED in practice grants an automatic filing extension to 31 December of the following year and may grant a further eight-month deferral upon justified request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the exercise comptable (fiscal year).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an SCSp: state the accounting period of the Luxembourg economic activity; do not include periods during which the entity was dormant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg national business registration number (numero de matricule), RCS (trade register) number, legal form code 'SCSp', and address of registered office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a Luxembourg tax identification number from the AED before filing; attach a proof of registration with the RCS for the Luxembourg establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax status and option declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of fiscal transparency under Art. 175bis LIR or confirmation that the SCSp has irrevocably opted to be subject to CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If transparent, no CIT is computed at SCSp level; the form must state that the partnership is a societe de personnes without separate taxable personality for income tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pre-tax accounting profit or loss per the Luxembourg GAAP balance sheet and profit and loss account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, enter zero at entity level and attach the allocation schedule identifying each partner's share; the e-commerce gross receipts from Stripe and PayPal must be fully reconciled to the accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs required by Art. 45-48 LIR and Art. 56 LIR: fines, penalties, excessive interest, related-party charges exceeding arm's length, 50% of representation costs, and taxes not deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The general partner or Luxembourg PE must recalculate transfer pricing limits on intercompany charges, including any group-level payment processing, marketing, or management fees embedded in the Stripe/PayPal commission base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5c - Deductions and IP box exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, the 80% IP income exemption (Art. 50bis LIR), the R&D credit (Art. 152quater LIR), and the investment tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A partner may claim the IP box relief only for qualifying IP assets held and economically used for the hydroponics retail activity; attach the patent, trademark, or software asset register and proof of income linkage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Allocation of taxable income to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of the total taxable base and its allocation pro rata to each partner; the schedule lists partner name, address, tax residence, capital share %, and allocated profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign partners must declare whether the allocated income is attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment, whether Luxembourg real estate is involved, and which double tax treaty provision applies; online sales via Stripe/PayPal alone do not create a Luxembourg PE for passive foreign partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - CIT and municipal business tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of CIT at 15%/16%/17% progressive bands, the 7% employment fund surcharge, and the communal trade tax (impot commercial communal) according to the municipality of the Luxembourg establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate partners compute CIT on their allocated share, reduce it by the participation exemption if the 10%/12-month conditions are met, and claim treaty relief where a DTA assigns the income to the partner's country of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Declarations of payments to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of management fees, commissions, interest, royalties, and other amounts paid to any foreign beneficiary exceeding EUR 2,500 per beneficiary in the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Luxembourg imposes no withholding tax on outbound interest or royalties; nonetheless, the schedule must identify the foreign recipient, its tax residence, and the nature of the service to support automatic exchange of information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the general partner (associe commandite) or its authorized Luxembourg representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident general partner must hold a valid LuxTrust certificate or grant a formal power of attorney to a Luxembourg-resident professional authorized to sign electronically.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers: (i) taxation d'office (arbitrary assessment) under Art. 8 LGI with a customary 10% uplift; (ii) late payment interest of 0.6% per month on the assessed amount; (iii) a coercive daily fine (astreinte) of up to EUR 250 per day ordered by the AED until the return is filed; (iv) criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 in repeated or aggravated cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 8002 - SCSp transparency information return (declaration d'attribution des resultats) filed through the same eCDF/MyGuichet.lu portal; this form is mandatory for a fiscally transparent SCSp even when no CIT is due at entity level.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same deadline as Form 8000: 31 May following the fiscal year-end, with the same practical extension practice to 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, RCS number, Luxembourg address, date of incorporation, and indication that the entity is not subject to CIT on a standalone basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The identification must match the RCS file; non-resident managers must list their residence address and foreign tax identification number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B - Accounting and fiscal result
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting result, fiscal adjustments, and final taxable result before allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The result must reconcile with the payments received through Stripe and PayPal; any discrepancy will be questioned under the AED digital-economy audit program.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C - Allocation schedule per partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner-by-partner allocation: full legal name, address, country of tax residence, profit-sharing percentage, allocated income or loss, and local tax identification number where available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign partners, state whether the allocated income is attributable to a Luxembourg PE; if not, confirm that the source of income is not Luxembourg real estate and that the applicable DTA assigns taxing rights to the partner's residence state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D - Withholding and payment declarations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of any Luxembourg-source interest, royalties, or director fees paid to partners or third parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that no Luxembourg withholding is due on interest or royalties; retain the underlying contracts, invoices, and beneficial ownership statements for six years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature by the general partner or authorized representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a LuxTrust digital certificate; a non-resident signatory may alternatively submit a notarized power of attorney to a Luxembourg fiscal representative.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the transparency return is treated as failure to file a tax return: official assessment with a 10% uplift, monthly interest of 0.6%, coercive fines of up to EUR 250 per day, and monetary sanctions from EUR 1,500 to EUR 25,000 for deficient or misleading partner allocation schedules.
